verses.1: A good name is chosen over great wealth, and over silver and gold, a good favor.
verses.2: The rich and the poor meet together — the LORD made them all.
verses.3: The wise man sees evil and hides, but the naive pass through and are punished.
verses.4: The reward of humility is the fear of the LORD — wealth and honor and life.
verses.5: Snares and traps are in crooked ways, and the one who guards his life keeps away from them.
verses.6: Train a child according to his way, and even when he grows old he will not depart from it.
verses.7: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
verses.8: The one who sows injustice reaps iniquity, and the rod of his wrongdoing will exhaust him.
verses.9: One who has a good eye is blessed — for he gives to the poor from his bread.
verses.10: Drive out the scoffer and contention will depart — then judgment and honor will remain.
verses.11: One who loves purity of heart and a good tongue, his neighbor is like a king.
verses.12: The eyes of the LORD guard knowledge, and He crushes the words of the deceiver.
verses.13: The lazy man says, “There is a lion in the street, in the middle of the squares I will be killed.”
verses.14: A deep pit is the mouth of a prostitute — the LORD abhors it; into it she will fall.
verses.15: Folly is bound in the heart of a youth — a rod of discipline will remove it from him.
verses.16: One who oppresses the poor to increase his wealth gives to the rich, but it only brings him need.
verses.17: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge.
verses.18: For if you keep them in your heart they will delight you together on your lips.
verses.19: That your trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to you today, even you.
verses.20: Have I not written to you in thirty sayings and wisdom and knowledge?
verses.21: To teach you the adornment of true words, to answer true words to those who send you.
verses.22: Do not rob the poor, for he is poor — nor insult the afflicted at the gate.
verses.23: For the LORD will plead their case, and He will establish the life of those who are oppressed.
verses.24: Do not associate with a man of quick temper, and do not be a companion to a wrathful man,
verses.25: lest you learn his ways and take a snare for your soul.
verses.26: Do not be among those who press claims in quarrels, bearing away their burdens.
verses.27: If you have nothing to pay, why should you take away your neighbor’s bed from beneath him?
verses.28: Do not move an ancient boundary that your fathers have set.
verses.29: Have you seen a man skilled in his work? He will stand before kings, he will not stand before obscure men.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: The Hebrew is difficult, but the reading follows "the mouth of a prostitute" as a metaphor for a seductive or dangerous source of temptation. The phrase "the LORD abhors it; into it she will fall" reflects the moral judgment and consequence.
- v. 16: The Hebrew implies a cycle of oppression and need — the rich man gives to the poor, but it only brings him more need. The nuance is preserved in the rendering.
